title: Ten Principles — good design, demonstrated
description: A tour of Dieter Rams's ten principles of good design, where each principle is a small experiment on an invented product, the Pell 3 kitchen timer. You count the actions needed to start a timer with and without remembered times, match features to real needs, align a layout and watch its edges and offsets fall, find Pause from symbols or labels, time yourself stopping an alarm with and without decoration, and read a battery gauge's lie factor. You also watch trendy styling date on a half-life, fix five small details, cut a year's energy use and remove parts until the timer stops working. It moves by keyboard, and every principle has a deep link.
prompt: Build Ten Principles, a tour of Dieter Rams's ten principles of good design. You can list the ten short principle names with attribution, but every explanation must be in your own words. Make each principle a small interactive demo on a generic product UI you invent, with a measurable state. For example, for 'unobtrusive', toggle away the decoration and watch the task time; for 'as little design as possible', remove elements until the function breaks. The tour should work from the keyboard and have a deep link for each principle via the hash. Give it a calm, product-like look of its own. Tests should check that all ten are present and in order, each demo's interaction and measurable state, keyboard navigation and deep links.

methodology: Order and content: the spec holds its own copy of the ten principle names in Rams's order and compares the rail, the section headings and data-principle order with it. Each explanation must be longer than 150 characters, must not repeat its heading, and must differ from the other nine.

Navigation as a user does it: real ArrowLeft, ArrowRight, Home and End presses, with bounds at 1 and 10 and focus moving to each heading. Arrows inside a slider change the slider, not the tour. Deep links (#principle-6), pushState history with goBack and goForward, reloads, hand-edited hashes and bad hashes that fall back to principle 1 are all checked.

Measured on the page, not taken from it: the aesthetic demo's left edges and mean offset are re-measured from getBoundingClientRect and halve exactly at 50% order. The honest demo's bar length is measured on screen and must equal √v, giving lie factors of 2.00, 1.25 and 3.33. The thorough demo's smallest touch target is measured before (under 44 px) and after (at least 44 px), and the focus ring and tabular digits are read from computed styles.

Hand-computed models: 13 actions against 1 for a 12-minute timer; a trend half-life of 0.5^(4/3 + 2), giving 90.1% dated after 4 years; energy of (0.6 + 8 × 0.6 + 15 × 0.5) Wh × 365 = 4.71 kWh a year falling to 0.64 kWh; ceil(10 / 2.5) = 4 timers a decade falling to 1; and a 4-part minimum that breaks when the dial goes.

Timing under page.clock: with the clock paused, the unobtrusive task is timed to the millisecond (2300 ms decorated, 800 ms plain), alongside the item counts (13 and 3) and the stated serial-search estimate (650 ms and 150 ms).
risks: The numbers behind several demos (100 ms per item searched, style half-lives, standby wattages, battery life) are illustrative assumptions. They are stated on the page, not measurements of any real product.
In the 'understandable' demo the symbol-only buttons are deliberately named 'Symbol 1–4' for assistive technology, to show the flaw honestly; the labelled mode fixes it.
The 'thorough' demo removes the focus ring on purpose until its checkbox is ticked; the rest of the page always shows focus.
The principle headings are quoted as widely cited; wording varies slightly between sources (for example 'environmentally friendly' with or without a hyphen).
qa.playwright: Most of the spec is plain clicks, fills and keyboard presses on the real controls, followed by web-first assertions on the readouts. Values that depend on layout (edges, bar length, target size) are measured in page.evaluate with getBoundingClientRect, so the checks would catch a CSS regression that the page's own state object missed. page.goBack and page.goForward exercised the pushState history, and location.hash assignment covered a hand-edited URL. The focus-ring check needed care: programmatic focus does not always match :focus-visible, so the spec focuses the first button and presses Tab to reach the second. page.clock.install with pauseAt and runFor made the task timer read exactly 2.30 s and 0.80 s. In this spec, no page bug came to light while I wrote it; the first full run was green except for runs cut off when a shared static server went away.
coverage: Ten names in order in the rail and the sections; unique original explanations
Keyboard tour, bounds, focus, sliders not hijacked
Deep links, history, reload, bad hashes
Aesthetic: measured edges and offsets; seeded disorder
Honest: on-screen bar length and lie factor
Long-lasting half-life, environment energy and units, thorough details, least design

a11y: The tour is a nav of real links (one per principle) with aria-current on the current one, plus Previous and Next buttons that disable at the ends. Arrow keys, Home and End move the tour except inside form controls, and focus moves to the new heading. Every demo uses labelled native checkboxes, ranges and buttons, toggles use aria-pressed, and each demo's verdict is an aria-live region. The deliberately weak controls in the understandable and thorough demos are explained on the page, and the fixed versions are one checkbox away.
